---
title: "Baselines and dependencies"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

A dossier compares two versions of a package, the baseline and the candidate. Both
are built from source the same way, installed into their own libraries and run
against the same dependencies. By default, the baseline is the CRAN release, the
candidate is the package folder you are in, and the dependencies are the packages
in your library. That answers the usual question before a release. This article
covers the others: other baselines, packages not on CRAN, and which versions of the
dependencies both versions run against.

## Where a version comes from

`dossier()` takes a source for each version:

| Source | The version | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `cran_release()` | on CRAN now | the baseline (the default) |
| `cran_version("1.0.0")` | a CRAN version, current or archived | an older baseline |
| `installed_version()` | in your library, fetched as source from CRAN | as a user, before upgrading |
| `tarball("mypkg_1.2.0.tar.gz")` | a source tarball on disk | a version you built or downloaded |
| `git_ref(".", "v1.2.0")` | a commit, branch or tag, as committed | packages not on CRAN; branches |
| `local_path(".")` | a package folder, as it is now | the candidate (the default) |

Describing a dossier reads and downloads nothing; `prepare_versions()`, which
`run_dossier()` calls first, fetches and builds both versions, and says what it
downloads before it does. A copy of the package installed in your library is never
used: `installed_version()` only says which version to fetch.

## Choosing the baseline

**The release your users have** is `cran_release()`, the default. Each call reads
CRAN's index, so a new release becomes the baseline as soon as the index lists it.

**An older release.** Many users skip releases, and upgrade from a version older
than the current one. To see what someone upgrading from 1.0.0 meets:

```{r}
run_dossier(dossier("mypkg", base = cran_version("1.0.0")))
```

The scenarios are then 1.0.0's vignettes and examples: the code those users learned
from.

**A package not on CRAN.** Compare with the git tag of the last release. When
`run_dossier()` finds no CRAN release, it names the repository's tags:

```{r}
run_dossier(dossier("mypkg", base = git_ref(".", "v0.3.0")))
```

**Two branches.** `git_ref()` exports only what is committed, with `git archive`,
and builds it in the work folder, never in the repository:

```{r}
run_dossier(dossier("mypkg", base = git_ref(".", "main"),
                    candidate = git_ref(".", "feature")))
```

For a package in a subfolder of its repository, give the subfolder:
`git_ref(".", "v1.0.0", subdir = "pkg")`, `local_path("pkg")`.

## Checking the baseline against its tag

A CRAN release is the tarball you uploaded, not necessarily the commit you tagged.
With `base_tag`, `prepare_versions()` checks that the baseline's `R/` folder matches
the tag (line endings aside) and counts the candidate's commits since:

```{r}
run_dossier(dossier("mypkg", base_tag = "v1.2.0"))
```

The report shows the result with the rest of the provenance: each version's sha256,
its `Packaged`, `Repository` and `Date/Publication` fields, and the git commit.

## Dependencies

Both versions always run against the same dependencies, so every labelled
difference comes from the package itself. `deps` chooses which dependencies those
are:

| `deps` | Both versions run against | Use it |
|---|---|---|
| `deps_shared()` | the packages in your library (the default) | the everyday run: fast, nothing installed |
| `deps_cran()` | today's CRAN versions, installed in the work folder | before a release: what a user installing today gets |
| `deps_snapshot()` | the versions CRAN had on the baseline's release date | to run the baseline as its users had it |

With `deps_cran()` and `deps_snapshot()`, the package's dependencies (`Depends`,
`Imports` and `LinkingTo`, recursively) are installed into the work folder. R's base
and recommended packages are used as installed, and packages only the scenarios use,
such as a vignette's suggested packages, come from your library.

```{r}
run_dossier(dossier("mypkg", deps = deps_cran()))
```

`deps_snapshot()` takes the versions from Posit Package Manager's dated snapshots.
For a baseline from git or a folder, whose packaging date is today, give the date:
`deps_snapshot("2025-06-10")`. A candidate that needs newer dependencies than the
snapshot has stops with a message. Under an R much newer than the snapshot, some old
versions no longer build; those are installed at their current version, and
`prepare_versions()` says which.

## When a dependency broke the release

A step that errors under both versions is a scenario problem: release code that
fails whichever version runs it. When the release once ran cleanly, a dependency may
have changed since: a function removed, a default changed. Run the dossier again
with `deps_snapshot()`. If the problem goes away, a change in a dependency broke
that code, for the release and for your new version alike.

## The work folder

Everything a dossier fetches, builds, installs and runs is kept in its work folder,
by default in `tempdir()`, which is gone when R ends. To keep the work between
sessions, give it a folder of its own:

```{r}
d <- dossier("mypkg", work = "~/dossiers/mypkg")
```

Keep it outside the package, or list it in `.Rbuildignore`: `R CMD build` would
otherwise copy it into every build. A version whose source has not changed is not
installed again, and runs are reused while nothing that shapes them has changed. The
dependency libraries are kept per R minor version (4.5, 4.6, ...), so using the same
folder under another R installs them afresh.
